newsitem.title: HUNGARY: POSITION LIQUIDATIONS DRIVE BCE SWISS FRANCS UP.
newsitem.headline: POSITION LIQUIDATIONS DRIVE BCE SWISS FRANCS UP.

text.p: Mostly strengthening Swiss francs and generally weaker yen futures remained the most actively traded contracts on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Tuesday, traders said.
"I guess many clients had selling positions and they could not undertake to further finance them, therefore these positions were liquidated," said Janos Fonodi of Termin Broker.
The most actively traded June Swiss francs firmed 1.83 fillers to 128.93, while the Swiss francs bucked the trend for December and dipped 0.25 fillers to 140.20.

"A weaker Euro can be expected if Italy and Spain join the EMU in the first round and this strengthens the Swiss francs, while the export oriented Swiss economy would need a weaker Swiss franc," Fonodi said.
Sterling futures strengthened on the back of denials in Britain of earlier rumours that sterling would rejoin the ERM and on outlook of a rate increase there, Fonodi said.
December sterling, for which most deals were made, rose one forint to 316 forints and the June maturity also put on 44 fillers.
Stronger dollar and weaker mark futures reflected changes on the spot market and reflected fading fears of a rate hike by the U.S. Fed's FOMC meeting on May 20, traders said.

On the Budapest Stock Exchange's currency section German mark futures saw active trade worth 1.27 billion forints with mostly stable prices. March and June 1998, for which deals were made, edged up 0.01 forints to 120.22 forints, and eased 2.79 forints to 123.71, respectively.
